CHAPTER III

WOMEN'S PROTECTION

Article 8

1. Women have the right to obtain protection from acts of  domestic violence, protection of women's rights in  employment, protection of women in emergency situations and special conditions  as well as protection of women's rights from criminal acts of human trafficking.
2. Protection of women's rights from acts of domestic violence  in the form of prevention of physical and psychological violence, sexual violence and neglect,  handling, services and empowerment of victims of domestic violence.
3. Protection of women's rights in employment rights inside or outside  the country to obtain protection in the prevention and handling of cases of  neglect of women's rights in terms of employment.
4. Protection of women's rights in emergency conditions and special conditions,  includes protection of women in emergency situations, in conflict areas,  disaster areas, protection of the rights of women with disabilities, and  protection of the rights of elderly women with social problems.
5. Protection of women's rights from acts of human trafficking includes  prevention and handling, services and empowerment of victims of criminal acts  of human trafficking.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regent is the Regent of Tasikmalaya. 2. Regency Area is the Regency Area of Tasikmalaya. 3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of regional government administration. 5. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regency DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Regency area. 6. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities. 7. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and children victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention efforts, services and social rehabilitation. 8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 9. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 11. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 12. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 13. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 14. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 15. Domestic Violence hereinafter referred to as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the scope of the household. 16. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 17. Guardian is a person or body who in reality exercises custody as a Parent over a Child. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 20. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service. 21. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the Tasikmalaya Regency area. 22. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanism of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 23. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who become victims of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect. 24. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 25. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or having occurred violence against victims. 26. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative of an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 27. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction in order to carry out social functions properly. 29. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 30. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Women and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPPA is a technical implementer to carry out operational technical activities in its working area in providing services for women and children experiencing problems of violence, discrimination, special protection and other problems; 31.

Article 32

1. The community as referred to in Article 29 letter c is obliged and responsible for the protection of women and children through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.
2. Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; andc. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.

CHAPTER XIII

SANCTIONS

Article 64

1. Any person who intentionally violates the provisions of Article 10 or fails to provide protection against forms of violence against women and children as referred to in Article 25 and Article 26, and fails to provide the rights of women and children as referred to in Article 27 and Article 28, thereby causing violence to occur, allowing violence to occur, and/or failing to report and failing to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in laws and regulations.
2. Regency Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of administering women's empowerment and child protection that fails to carry out its obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.
3. Management of P2TP2A, Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children at Sub-District Level, Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children at Village Level and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection duties, if violating protection principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within the internal institutions or respective organizations.

Article 33

1. Parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in Article 29 letter d legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and report if violence occurs and protect victims.
2. In the event that parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in paragraph (1) do not exist or their whereabouts are unknown or due to a certain reason cannot carry out their obligations and responsibilities, then the obligations and responsibilities may be transferred to the Regional Government and other family members implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Paragraph 6

Protection of Child Victims of Physical and/or Mental Violence and Children with Disabilities

Article 31

1. The village government as referred to in Article 29 letter b, is obliged and responsible to:a. formulate and implement programs and activities related to the protection of women and children;
b. implement the protection of women and children from violence;c. realize a Child-Friendly village; andd. allocate budget for the protection of women and children from violence according to village financial capacity in each fiscal year.
2. In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the village government formulates programs and activities for the protection of women and children in the village action plan which is part of the village medium-term development plan.

Part Six

Child Protection in the Social Field

1. Making policies for the protection of child victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse; 2. Making special protection policies for children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse; and

b. Risk Reduction Services, which include:
1. Conducting early identification, complaint services and assessment of children and families at risk;
2. Providing services for children and families who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse including:a. guidance and counseling on parenting patterns and behavior change;
b. legal consultation; andc. psychosocial services.
c. Case Handling Services, including:
1. Conducting immediate rescue efforts for victims who are in dangerous conditions for their safety;
2. Providing referrals according to the needs of victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse; 3. Conducting counseling and support from the family; 4. Treating child victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse in a humane manner in accordance with the dignity and rights of children; and
5. Providing rehabilitation and social reintegration services.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regent is the Regent of Tasikmalaya. 2. Regency Area is the Regency Area of Tasikmalaya. 3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of regional government administration. 5. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regency DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Regency area. 6. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities. 7. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and children victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention efforts, services and social rehabilitation. 8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 9. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 11. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 12. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 13. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 14. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 15. Domestic Violence hereinafter referred to as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the scope of the household. 16. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 17. Guardian is a person or body who in reality exercises custody as a Parent over a Child. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 20. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service. 21. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the Tasikmalaya Regency area. 22. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanism of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 23. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who become victims of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect. 24. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 25. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or having occurred violence against victims. 26. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative of an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 27. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction in order to carry out social functions properly. 29. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 30. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Women and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPPA is a technical implementer to carry out operational technical activities in its working area in providing services for women and children experiencing problems of violence, discrimination, special protection and other problems; 31.

Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive. 32. CHAPTER XI

MONITORING, EVALUATION, AND REPORTING

Article 60

Monitoring is conducted regularly and in an integrated manner every 6 (six) months by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in coordination with Regional Apparatus or other units handling women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 55

1. The Village Level Children's Forum as referred to in Article 52 paragraph (2) letter c constitutes a forum for children's participation within the Village area with membership consisting of representatives from Neighbourhood Units and Community Units of at least 1 (one) girl and 1 (one) boy.
2. The Village Level Children's Forum is established by Decree of the Village Head with a term of office of 2 (two) years.
3. The Village Government as Supervisor of the Village Level Children's Forum facilitates the formation of the Village Level Children's Forum starting from the selection stage, ratification of management and guidance in capacity building of members of the Village Level Children's Forum.
4. Community institutions existing in the Village have the obligation to accommodate and foster children's participation in development as well as in advocating for children's rights.

CHAPTER XIII

SANCTIONS

Article 64

1. Any person who intentionally violates the provisions of Article 10 or fails to provide protection against forms of violence against women and children as referred to in Article 25 and Article 26, and fails to provide the rights of women and children as referred to in Article 27 and Article 28, thereby causing violence to occur, allowing violence to occur, and/or failing to report and failing to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in laws and regulations.
2. Regency Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of administering women's empowerment and child protection that fails to carry out its obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.
3. Management of P2TP2A, Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children at Sub-District Level, Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children at Village Level and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection duties, if violating protection principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within the internal institutions or respective organizations.

Article 32

CHAPTER III

WOMEN'S PROTECTION

Article 8

1. Women have the right to obtain protection from acts of  domestic violence, protection of women's rights in  employment, protection of women in emergency situations and special conditions  as well as protection of women's rights from criminal acts of human trafficking.
2. Protection of women's rights from acts of domestic violence  in the form of prevention of physical and psychological violence, sexual violence and neglect,  handling, services and empowerment of victims of domestic violence.
3. Protection of women's rights in employment rights inside or outside  the country to obtain protection in the prevention and handling of cases of  neglect of women's rights in terms of employment.
4. Protection of women's rights in emergency conditions and special conditions,  includes protection of women in emergency situations, in conflict areas,  disaster areas, protection of the rights of women with disabilities, and  protection of the rights of elderly women with social problems.
5. Protection of women's rights from acts of human trafficking includes  prevention and handling, services and empowerment of victims of criminal acts  of human trafficking.

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT

Article 2

1. The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility for the implementation of women's empowerment.

Article 9

CHAPTER XIII

SANCTIONS

Article 64

1. Any person who intentionally violates the provisions of Article 10 or fails to provide protection against forms of violence against women and children as referred to in Article 25 and Article 26, and fails to provide the rights of women and children as referred to in Article 27 and Article 28, thereby causing violence to occur, allowing violence to occur, and/or failing to report and failing to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in laws and regulations.

3. Management of P2TP2A, Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children at Sub-District Level, Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children at Village Level and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection duties, if violating protection principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within the internal institutions or respective organizations.

Article 32

1. The community as referred to in Article 29 letter c is obliged and responsible for the protection of women and children through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.
2. Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; andc. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.

CHAPTER XIII

SANCTIONS

Article 64

1. Any person who intentionally violates the provisions of Article 10 or fails to provide protection against forms of violence against women and children as referred to in Article 25 and Article 26, and fails to provide the rights of women and children as referred to in Article 27 and Article 28, thereby causing violence to occur, allowing violence to occur, and/or failing to report and failing to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in laws and regulations.
2. Regency Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of administering women's empowerment and child protection that fails to carry out its obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.
3. Management of P2TP2A, Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children at Sub-District Level, Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children at Village Level and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection duties, if violating protection principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within the internal institutions or respective organizations.

Article 32

1. The community as referred to in Article 29 letter c is obliged and responsible for the protection of women and children through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.
2. Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; andc. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.

Article 21

1. Supervision, prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation of children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse as referred to in Article 17 letter d and involved in their production and distribution, is the obligation and responsibility of the Regional Government and the community.
2. The implementation of protection for children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in the form of:a. Prevention Services, including:
1. Making policies for the protection of child victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse; 2. Making special protection policies for children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse; and
3. Providing socialization and raising awareness of parents and/or the community and children regarding the adverse effects of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse.
b. Risk Reduction Services, which include:
1. Conducting early identification, complaint services and assessment of children and families at risk;
2. Providing services for children and families who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse including:a. guidance and counseling on parenting patterns and behavior change;
b. legal consultation; andc. psychosocial services.
c. Case Handling Services, including:
1. Conducting immediate rescue efforts for victims who are in dangerous conditions for their safety;
2. Providing referrals according to the needs of victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse; 3. Conducting counseling and support from the family; 4. Treating child victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse in a humane manner in accordance with the dignity and rights of children; and
5. Providing rehabilitation and social reintegration services.

Article 33

1. Parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in Article 29 letter d legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and report if violence occurs and protect victims.
2. In the event that parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in paragraph (1) do not exist or their whereabouts are unknown or due to a certain reason cannot carry out their obligations and responsibilities, then the obligations and responsibilities may be transferred to the Regional Government and other family members implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 34

Regional Government carries out activities for the implementation of women's protection and child protection, which include:
a. prevention;
b. services; and c. social rehabilitation.

Article 31

1. The village government as referred to in Article 29 letter b, is obliged and responsible to:a. formulate and implement programs and activities related to the protection of women and children;
b. implement the protection of women and children from violence;c. realize a Child-Friendly village; andd. allocate budget for the protection of women and children from violence according to village financial capacity in each fiscal year.
2. In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the village government formulates programs and activities for the protection of women and children in the village action plan which is part of the village medium-term development plan.

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities. 7. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and children victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention efforts, services and social rehabilitation. 8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 9. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 11. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 12. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 14. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 15. Domestic Violence hereinafter referred to as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the scope of the household. 16. Guardian is a person or body who in reality exercises custody as a Parent over a Child. 18. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the Tasikmalaya Regency area. 22. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanism of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 23. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who become victims of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect. 24. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 25. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or having occurred violence against victims. 26. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative of an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 27. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction in order to carry out social functions properly. 29. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 30. Any person who intentionally violates the provisions of Article 10 or fails to provide protection against forms of violence against women and children as referred to in Article 25 and Article 26, and fails to provide the rights of women and children as referred to in Article 27 and Article 28, thereby causing violence to occur, allowing violence to occur, and/or failing to report and failing to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in laws and regulations.
2. Regency Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of administering women's empowerment and child protection that fails to carry out its obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.
3. Management of P2TP2A, Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children at Sub-District Level, Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children at Village Level and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection duties, if violating protection principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within the internal institutions or respective organizations.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regent is the Regent of Tasikmalaya. 2. Regency Area is the Regency Area of Tasikmalaya. 3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of regional government administration. 5. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regency DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Regency area. 6. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities. 7. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and children victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention efforts, services and social rehabilitation. 8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 9. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 11. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 12. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 13. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 14. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 15. Domestic Violence hereinafter referred to as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the scope of the household. 16. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 17. Guardian is a person or body who in reality exercises custody as a Parent over a Child. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 20. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service. 21. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the Tasikmalaya Regency area. 22. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanism of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 23. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who become victims of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect. 24. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 25. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or having occurred violence against victims. 26. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative of an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 27. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction in order to carry out social functions properly. 29. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 30. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Women and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPPA is a technical implementer to carry out operational technical activities in its working area in providing services for women and children experiencing problems of violence, discrimination, special protection and other problems; 31.

1. Conducting immediate rescue efforts for victims who are in dangerous conditions for their safety;

CHAPTER III

WOMEN'S PROTECTION

Article 8

1. Women have the right to obtain protection from acts of  domestic violence, protection of women's rights in  employment, protection of women in emergency situations and special conditions  as well as protection of women's rights from criminal acts of human trafficking.
2. Protection of women's rights from acts of domestic violence  in the form of prevention of physical and psychological violence, sexual violence and neglect,  handling, services and empowerment of victims of domestic violence.
3. Protection of women's rights in employment rights inside or outside  the country to obtain protection in the prevention and handling of cases of  neglect of women's rights in terms of employment.
4. Protection of women's rights in emergency conditions and special conditions,  includes protection of women in emergency situations, in conflict areas,  disaster areas, protection of the rights of women with disabilities, and  protection of the rights of elderly women with social problems.
5. Protection of women's rights from acts of human trafficking includes  prevention and handling, services and empowerment of victims of criminal acts  of human trafficking.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regent is the Regent of Tasikmalaya. 2. Regency Area is the Regency Area of Tasikmalaya. 3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of regional government administration. 5. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regency DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Regency area. 6. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities. 7. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and children victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention efforts, services and social rehabilitation. 8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 9. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 11. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 12. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 13. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 14. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 15. Domestic Violence hereinafter referred to as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the scope of the household. 16. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 17. Guardian is a person or body who in reality exercises custody as a Parent over a Child. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 20. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service. 21. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the Tasikmalaya Regency area. 22. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanism of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 23. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who become victims of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect. 24. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 25. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or having occurred violence against victims. 26. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative of an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 27. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction in order to carry out social functions properly. 29. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 30. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Women and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPPA is a technical implementer to carry out operational technical activities in its working area in providing services for women and children experiencing problems of violence, discrimination, special protection and other problems; 31.
